findings.issue: A-4 / §5 say the initial Home must not move focus (only Home reached via Cancel/← Home focuses its h1). No test asserts this.
findings.evidence: Mutant in src/ui/useHeadingFocus.ts:11 removing the `!enabled ||` guard (focus always) left all 7 home.spec.ts tests passing in Chromium. The Cancel/Config/Table focus mutants were all caught.
findings.fix: In the launch test, after openHome, add `await expect(heading(page, 'TLH Trainer')).not.toBeFocused();` (or check `document.activeElement === document.body`).

findings.issue: D-4 has the Table read the user's hole cards from table.config.userSeat, but nothing renders the Table with a non-default user seat, so going back to the constant 5 would not be caught.
findings.evidence: Mutant `p.seat === 5` at Table.tsx:16 survived every Vitest suite. The e2e tests only use the default seat 5.
findings.fix: Add one renderToString assertion (e.g. in tests/table/session-config.test.ts or a UI test) that renders `<Table config={{ userSeat: 2, button: 3, seats: SWAPPED }} />`, or a pure check on the seated table, and confirms the user row is the You seat at 2. Or note D-4 for Table.tsx as covered only by review.

findings.issue: The shallow `{ ...DEFAULT_SESSION_CONFIG, ...input }` merge can produce inconsistent configs. `seatSession({ userSeat: 2 })` makes seat 2 (Ben, a bot) the user: nextStep returns 'user' on Ben's turn. `seatSession({ seats: fourSeats })` keeps players 6 and button 6. Without exactOptionalPropertyTypes, `{ stake: undefined }` also type-checks and crashes in buyIn. Spec A-11/F-4 accept this (the only producer is DEFAULT_SESSION_CONFIG, and the only partial callers pass stake alone), so this is not a spec violation.
findings.evidence: session.ts:92-94 resolveSessionConfig. tsconfig.json has no exactOptionalPropertyTypes.
findings.fix: No change needed this slice. Make sure F-4 (assertSessionConfig) also covers userSeat matching the 'user' seat, players === seats.length and the button being one of the seats, and consider narrowing callers to `Pick<SessionConfig,'stake'>` when TASK-2.2+ adds real producers.

findings.issue: `stacks: config.seats.map(...)` going back to DEFAULT_SEATS is an equivalent mutant for the worked example, because SWAPPED keeps seat numbers 1-6.
findings.fix: Optional: add `expect(seatSession({ seats: SWAPPED.slice(0, 5), players: 5 }).stacks.map(s => s.seat)).toEqual([1,2,3,4,5])` or similar.

findings.issue: TABLE_SIZE_NAMES has 'heads-up' and 'full ring' entries, and playersLabel has a fallback branch. Neither can be reached while players is fixed at 6 (selectors are TASK-2.2). The labels do come from the storyboard, though.
findings.evidence: Config.dc.html contains '2 (heads-up)' and '10 (full ring)'. In this slice only 6 is rendered.
findings.fix: Optional: inline '6 (6-max)' via a one-entry map until TASK-2.2, or keep it as is.

summary:
All 17 SPEC items are implemented and tested. SessionConfig matches Q-2 field for field. The Table really uses config.seats, config.button and config.userSeat in seatSession, dealHand, nextStep, applyUserAction, completedHand, userActionBar and Table.tsx, and session/action-bar mutants of each were caught by session-config.test.ts. No session starts before Start game: the Table mounts only on the 'table' screen, and e2e checks the draw count stays 0. Cancel and ← Home store nothing; storage and history lengths are checked. The cross-story diff is exactly the four Q-3 edits: two lines in each openApp, the import and render swap in table.acceptance, and app.test rewritten. The builder's departures are sound. useHeadingFocus is used by three screens; it sets tabIndex at runtime because the spec's `

` would contradict the locked `

TLH Trainer

` assertion. The optional preload is real React 19 SSR output (confirmed: ``), and the app-test mutants were still caught. The SPEC-02 substitute (the bundle references exactly one JPEG, which is the Home URL, plus the card-gallery logo bytes match the served bytes) is needed because the in-app Table renders no card backs, and it is at least as strong. The Session panel's visually hidden h2 is what spec §5 says, and it matches the storyboard, which has no visible Session heading either. The ← Home link uses #FF6B70 (6.93:1 on #0E0F12, hover #FF9A9D), not #D7262E. #D7262E is used only as a background behind white text (4.99:1). Full e2e passed in a scratch copy (60/60, Chromium and WebKit), and the scratch copy has been deleted. No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings.
